sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Aíbgréne is an Irish heroine. In some texts she is the daughter of the doomed lovers Deirdre and Noísiu. Her name is also written Abgrenia. She is otherwise unknown in the sources. The tale of her parents is one of the best-known stories of the Ulster cycle. Deirdre and Noísiu were fated lovers who fled Ireland together. They lived in exile until their return brought betrayal. Both met their death as a result. The tradition names Aíbgréne as the fruit of that tragic union. Her single appearance adds a descendant to the doomed family line.

okr.objective: This article establishes Aíbgréne as an obscure Irish heroine named as the daughter of the doomed lovers Deirdre and Noísiu.
